FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Utensils, 
Cutlery Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Divisional 
Council. 


An insulated flask is an insulated storage vessel that greatly lengthens the time over which its hot or cold content 
remain hotter or cooler than the flask’s surroundings. The gap between the two flasks is stuffed with food grade 
insulated material which significantly reduces heat transfer by conduction or convection. 


While preparing this standard, assistance has been taken from BS EN 12546-1 : 2000 “Materials and articles in 
contact with foodstuffs. Insulated containers for domestic use: Part I Specification for vacuum ware, insulated 
flasks and jugs’. While implementing this standard, the manufacturer shall ensure compliance with relevant 
statutory regulations. 


The relevant SI units and corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance: 
Pressure 1Pa (Pascal) = 1 N/m? 
I kgf/mm? = 9.806 65 MPa 
The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex C. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17790 : 2022 


Indian Standard 


INSULATED FLASK FOR 
DOMESTIC USE — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard covers minimum requirements of 
domestic insulated stainless steel flask for storage and 
maintaining the temperature of hot and cold liquids 
used for drinking purpose. 


1.2 The flask will have stainless steel inner container. 
The outer container may be of stainless steel or plastic. 


NOTE — The flask can be for transporting or table top. 


2 REFERENCES

valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties

to investigate possibility of applying the most recent

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Domestic Stainless Steel Insulated Flask — Flask 
having two containers having food grade insulating 
material in between, consisting of either: 


a) Both outer and inner containers stainless steel; or 


b) Outer container food grade plastic and inner 
stainless steel container. 


3.1.1 Normally, the mouth portion of the flask may be 
narrow or wide for storage or transporting of hot and 
cold liquid used for drinking. 


3.2 Nominal Capacity — Volume of water at room 
temperature required to fill the inner container, when in 
upright position, to a level 10 mm below the lowest part 
of the inserted closure. 


3.3 Table Top Use — Flask generally provided with a 
handle. 


3.4 Use for Transportation — Flask is normally 
provided with a strap, cord or handle. 


4 TYPES (SHAPE, SIZE AND 
CAPACITY) 


NOMINAL 


The stainless-steel insulated flasks normally comes 
in various capacities from 150 ml to 2 500 ml. The 
mouth portion (size) comes in typically following two 
variants: 


a) Wide mouth above 45 mm; and 


b) Narrow mouth 45 mm and below. 


NOTE — The design of the flask shall be such that it is easy to 
clean and prevent accumulation of dirt/muck. 


S MANUFACTURE AND WORKMANSHIP 


The shape, size and nominal capacity of the inner 
container shall be as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer. However, the nominal capacity 


IS 17790 : 2022 


of the inner container shall be declared by the 
manufacturer. 


5.1 The flask shall be clean, reasonably free from 
distortion, dents, wrinkles, wavy surface, colouring, 
burrs, scratches, pitting, deep tool marks and other 
surface defects. The design of the flask shall be such 
that, it is easy to clean and prevent accumulation of dirt. 


5.2 The flasks shall be subjected shall be subjected to 
tests as specified in 7. 


5.3 Welding if done, shall be free from welding defects. 
The welding electrode shall conform to grade 308 or 
higher grade as per IS 5856. The weld shall be finished 
properly, so that when a finger is passed on the Joint, it 
shall be smooth. 


5.4 Suitable handle or arrangement for suspension may 
be provided on a stainless steel insulated flask. 


6 SAMPLING 


For the purpose of conducting the tests, 3 samples 
of flask of each individual size shall be tested. In the 
event of I of the 3 samples failing the test, additional 
7 samples shall be tested and these shall all pass. 


7 REQUIREMENTS AND TESTS 


7.1 Materials 


7.1.1 Inner Containers 


The material used to manufacture the inner container 
shall be stainless steel of grade 304 or higher grade as 
per IS 5522. 


7.1.2 Outer Protective Case and Accessories 


Outer protective case and accessories shall be of 
materials which shall be rigid enough to hold the inner 
container securely under conditions of use, corrosion 
resistant and protect it from damage in normal handling. 


7.1.2.1 The material used for the outer container shall 
be of stainless steel as per N2 of IS 15997 or 304 series 
or higher according to IS 5522. The minimum thickness 
of the outer container shall be 0.3 mm for flasks with 
capacity less than I 000 ml and 0.4 mm for flasks with 
capacity 1 000 ml and above. 


7.1.2.2 Plastic casing 


The material used shall be food grade plastic, free from 
bisphenol A (BPA) and shall have a minimum thickness 
of 1.5 mm. 


7.1.3 The flask, if coated fully or partially externally, 
shall conform to the thickness test, salt water corrosion 
test, adhesion test procedures as per IS 9730. The limit 
for lead and cadmium of the coating shall be as per 
IS 9806 (see 51 No. iv) and v) of Table 1 of IS 9806) 


when measured as per standard test method. The 
minimum thickness of the coating shall be declared by 
the manufacturer. 


7.1.4 Stopper 


7.1.4.1 The stopper of the inner container shall be of 
non-toxic and food grade material (see IS 9845). If 
stainless steel is used, it shall conform to the material 
specified for the inner container (see 7.1.1). When fitted 
to the inner container, it shall not slip off and shall 
provide a leak proof fitting. The insulation material, if 
used inside the stopper shall be food grade. 


7.1.4.2 If O-ring or washer is provided, it shall be made 
of food grade silicone, refer to IS 3565 for information 
on silicone. 


7.1.4.3 The O-ring or washer, when visually examined, 
shall be free from blisters, pinholes, cracks, embedded 
foreign matters and other defects which may impair 
their serviceability. No joints are allowed 


NOTES 
1 Silicone manufacturer’s certificate for food grade is 
acceptable. 


2 Only physical and chemical properties of needs to be 
complied with for silicone O-ring or washer. 


7.1.5 Auxiliary Closure 


The auxiliary closure(s), also intended for use as 
drinking cup(s), shall be non-toxic, food grade 
material and shall not deform under normal conditions 
of use (see IS 9845). The materials shall not contain 
bisphenol A (BPA). 


7.2 Capacity Test 


7.2.1 The nominal capacity of flask may be declared 
one amongst 150 ml to 2 500 ml. Other capacities 
may be as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. The tolerance on the nominal capacity 
shall be + 5 percent. No negative tolerance is permitted. 


7.2.2 Volume of water at room temperature required to 
fill the insulated container, when in an upright position, 
to a level 10 mm below the lowest part of the inserted 
closure. 


7.2.2.1 Ensure the flask in empty. Take water in a 
calibrated jar. Pour the water from the calibrated jar 
into the flask, to a level 10 mm below the lowest part of 
the inserted closure. The difference in reading of water 
level in the calibrated jar is the capacity of the flask. 


7.3 Test for Heat Retention Capability 


The temperature of water heated to 95 °C (+ 1 *C/-0 °C) 
and kept in flask, in accordance with the method 
prescribed in Annex A, when measured at intervals of 
1, 6, 12 and 24 h respectively, shall be not less than as 
given in Table 1.

I h, 6 h and 12 h. For type testing, the flask shall be 
tested for 24 h. 


7.4 Test for Cold Retention Capability 

The temperature of water cooled to 5 °C and kept in 
flask, in accordance with the method prescribed in 
Annex B when measured after 6 h, shall be not greater 
than as given in Table 2.

7.5 Impact Resistance Test 
7.5.1 Drop Impact Test 


7.5.1.1 Fill water in the inner container up to its full 
capacity at the normal temperature and drop it from the 
height of 400 mm in а vertical state on a hard wood 
board of 30 mm or more in thickness fixed horizontally 
(see Fig. 1). 


7.5.1.2 The flask shall be free from defects harmful to 
use. There shall be no defects such as water leakage, 
crack, etc. on the flask and comply to heat or cold 
retention capacity as specified in 7.3 or 7.4 respectively. 


7.5.2 Pendulum Impact Test 


7.5.2.1 Fill water in the flask up to its full capacity at 
the normal temperature. Raise the flask to the position 
of 45 degrees by making the length of the shoulder 
strap 400 mm as shown in Fig. 2 and make the flask 
collide with a hard wood board of 30 mm or more in 
thickness fixed vertically. 


7.5.2.2 The flask shall be free from defects harmful to 
use. There shall be no defects, such as water leakage, 
crack, etc. on the flask and comply with heat or cold 
retention capacity as specified in 7.3 or 7.4 respectively. 


7.6 Test for Fixing Strength of the Handle 


7.6.1 A handle if provided on the flask, shall be 
subjected to the test as given in 7.6.1.1. 


7.6.1.1 Weigh the flask with water filled to its maximum 
capacity along with the stopper and cup. Gradually 
apply a load equal to a minimum of six times its mass 
as shown in Fig. 3. After the maximum load is attained. 
Keep the load for 5 min and examine the presence of 
any abnormality. 


7.6.2 The flask and handle shall be free from any 
abnormality after the test. 


7.7 Test for Strength of Shoulder Strap 


7.7.1 A shoulder strap if provided, shall be subjected to 
the test as given in 7.7.1.1. 


7.7.1.1 Weigh the flask with water filled to its 
maximum capacity along with the stopper(s) and 
cup(s). Apply a load, equal to a minimum of ten times 
its mass as shown in Fig. 4. After the maximum load is 
attained, keep for 5 min and examine the presence of 
any abnormality.

IS 17790 : 2022 


IS 17790 : 2022 


7.7.2 After/during this test, the strap shall not break. 
The area on the flask to which the strap is fastened shall 
not show any signs of damage or defect. The elongation 
under load shall not exceed 10 percent of the total length 
of the strap. Initial stretching due to unwinding of the 
strap shall not be taken as elongation for the purpose of 
calculation. 


NOTE — The material of the strap may be flexible and shall not 
be affected by water. 


7.8 Test for Strength of Cord 


7.8.1 In case instead of a shoulder strap, a cord is 
provided to tag the bottle to a hook, the strength of the 
cord shall be subjected to the test as given in 7.8.1.1. 


7.8.1.1 Take a random sample other than that specified in 
6. Put small steel balls equivalent to 3 times the weight 
(volume/capacity) of water that flask can hold. Hang the 
filled flask by a suitable means for 30 min. Ensure that 
flask is hanging freely without touching any surface. 


7.8.2 After/during this test, the cord shall not break. The 
area on the flask to which the cord is fastened shall not 
show any signs of damage or defect. The elongation 
under load shall not exceed 10 percent of the total length 
of the cord. Initial stretching due to unwinding of the 
cord shall not be taken as elongation for the purpose of 
calculation. 


NOTE — The material of the cord may be flexible and shall not 
be affected by water. 


7.9 Leakage Test 


Fill the flask to 75 percent of its nominal capacity with 
water at 95 *C containing 0.5 percent surfactant. Close 
the stopper with a torque of 2 Nm or, if not fitted with 
a screwed stopper, push in the stopper to its full extent. 
Thoroughly dry the outside of the stopper, spout and 
outer protective casing (container). Put the flask upside 
down position for at least 10 min. No drops shall appear 
on the stopper, spout, casing or on the surface on which 
the flask has been over turned. The flask shall be tested 
without the cup, if the flask is provided with a cup along 
with the stopper 


7.10 Joint Leakage Test 


The empty flask without stopper or plug or lever shall 
be weighed (weigh balance accuracy up to 10 mg). The 
flask shall be dipped fully in a water bath for at least 
5 min. After taking out the flask, the inside and outside of 
the flask shall be wipe dried. The flask shall be weighed 
again. There shall be no increase in weight of the flask. 


7.11 Staining Test 


The inner and outer surface of the flask shall be 
thoroughly washed with hot soapy water. Thoroughly 
rinse and then degrease the test specimens in acetone 
or methylated spirits, then wiped using a soft cloth. The 
flask, when dipped for 16 h in each of the following 


solutions maintained at 60 + 2 °C temperature, shall 
not show any sign of staining after removal from the 
solutions at the end of above period: 


a) Ten gram of glacial acetic acid (99 percent) 
dissolved in distilled water to make 100 ml; and 


b) Five gram of pure sodium chloride dissolved in 
distilled water to make 100 ml. 


7.12 Check for PUF (Polyurethane Foam) or Any 
Other Similar Thermal Insulation Material 


Separate sample other than as specified in 6 is taken and 
cut to check the declared insulating material. The same 
sample can be used for checking of container thickness 


7.13 Seepage Test 


7.13.1 Fill the flask up to 25 percent with blue coloured 
water (water with blue indelible ink). Close the flask 
with stopper and cup and shake the flask up and down 
through a distance of 200 mm + 50 mm, 25 times in 
15+2s. 

7.13.2 Empty the flask, dry wipe all the exposed 
surfaces. Dismantle or cut apart the flask and stopper 
to assess any seepage into the insulation material. There 
shall be no seepage. 


7.14 Lever, Device for Operating or Regulating Flow 
Test 


Operate the lever or device 1 500 times and check 
for proper functioning, its intended use as per the 
instructions of the manufacturer 


7.15 Test for Length of the Shoulder Strap 


The length of the shoulder strap, if provided, shall be 
400 mm or over when measured as given in Fig. 5 and 
the length of strap shall be adjustable. 


7.16 Test for Stability of Flask 


When the flask filled with water to the full capacity is 
placed upright over a rough 10* inclined plane, it shall 
not overturn or fall. 


7.17 Pour Test 


7.17.1 For purpose of this test, the flask shall be 3/44 
filled. A cup with a month opening of 60 mm to 80 mm 
diameter is placed approximately in the centre, above 
a sheet of white paper of 200 mm x 200 mm. When 
a black tea or coffee is poured out of the flask from a 
height of around 50 mm, measured from the pouring 
edge of the flask to the edge of the cup placed on the 
white paper, no stains caused by the sputtering shall 
appear on the white paper. 


7.17.2 No spluttering shall occur when liquid is poured 
out of the flask. 


NOTE — After all tests are performed, the sample flask which 
was tested should pass the leakage test.

8 INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE 


8.1 Flask shall carry adequate instructions to the user 
for its proper use to ensure satisfactory performance. 


8.2 The manufacturer shall provide the following 
minimum information along with each flask as given 
below: 

a) How to unpack and take care of environment; 

b) How to stock the flask in case the flask is not 
going to be used, to avoid pitting or getting 
contaminated; 

c) Wash thoroughly before and after use; 

d) Always rinse with clean water (preferably warm 
water) before each use; 

e) Ensure the flask is cleaned, empty and dry before 
stocking after each use; 

f) Do not use for carrying ice cubes; 

g) Do not use to store or carry carbonated drinks; 

h) In order to minimize bacterial growth, do not 
use to keep warm milk products or baby food 
for long. Follow instructions at b), c) above and 
ensure dry before using warm milk or baby food. 


The flask should not stink and should be properly 
sterilized first with hot water and later rinsed with 
RO/purified drinking water. Ensure the flask is dry 
and does not stink; 

j) The flask should be periodically cleaned; 

k) Never use in a dishwasher, unless otherwise stated 
by the manufacturer; 

m) Never use the flask, if there is suspected leakage 
between the two containers. Empty the flask and 
shake the flask there should be no sound of water 
in between the containers; 

n) Handle the flask carefully, do not drop the flask; 
and 


p) Keep these instructions safe. 
9 MARKING 


9.1 Each insulated stainless steel flask shall be legibly 
and permanently marked with the following minimum 
information: 

a) Declared nominal capacity; 


b) Grade of material of inner container and outer 
container along with applicable IS No; 


IS 17790 : 2022 


c) Name or trade mark of the manufacturer; 
d) Batch number; and 
e) Type of insulation used. 


9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 


Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10 PACKAGING 


Each insulated container shall be suitable packaged to 
avoid any damage during transit. The packaging shall 
be eco-friendly. 


IS 17790 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 7.3) 
TEST FOR HEAT RETENTION CAPACITY 


A-1 GENERAL 


The heat retention capacity of an insulated flask 
is determined by filling hot water at 95 °C in it, as 
prescribed in A-2 and measuring the temperature of 
water at intervals of 1, 6, 12 and 24 h, respectively. 
While carrying out the test, maintain the atmospheric 
conditions at 27 + 2 °C and 65 + 5 percent RH. The 
samples are to be pre-conditioned at 95 + 2 °C for a 
minimum period of 2 h before starting the test. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 Rinse the flask with water at 95 + 2 °C , drain 
out water. Quickly fill with boiling water. Allow the 


temperature to drop slowly to 95 °C. Close the flask 
with stopper and cup and note the time. Note the 
temperature of water in the flask at the end of 1, 6, 12 
or 24h respectively from the time the water in the flask 
attained the temperature of 95 °C. 


NOTES — In no case shall the flask be disturbed or opened 
except for measuring the temperature as stated above. 


A-2.2 The flask shall be taken as having passed the test, 
if the temperatures measured at the end of 1, 6, 12 and 
24 h are not less than those specified in 7.3. 


ANNEX B 
( Clause 7.4) 
TEST FOR COLD RETENTION CAPACITY 


B-1 GENERAL 


The cold retention capacity of a flask is determined 
by filling cold water at 5 °C in it, as prescribed in B-2 
and measuring the temperature of water after 6 h. The 
samples shall be pre-conditioned at 5 + I °C for a 
minimum period of 2 h before starting the test. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Rinse the flask with water at 5 + 1 °C, drain out 
water. Quickly fill flask up to the neck with ice cold 


water. Allow the temperature to increase slowly to 
5 °C. Close the flask with the stopper and cup and note 
the time. Note the temperature of water in the flask at 
the end of 6 h. 

NOTE — In no case shall the flask be disturbed or opened 


except for measuring the temperature as stated above. 


B-2.2 The flask shall be taken as having passed the test 
if the temperature measured at the end of 6 h shall not 
be greater than that specified in 7.4.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 33 (16197).
